svg.title: Engineering Kit: five parts, four layers, three commands
svg.desc: The Engineering Kit in three views. Top: the five parts, which say what the kit contains: Rule registry, Validators, Skills with evals, Evidence schema and Adapters. They are joined through rule identifiers: validators, skills and evidence records name the rules in the registry. Left: the four layers, which say who may change what, stacked from the shared core at the top to project configuration at the bottom. Arrows between the layers show that each layer may narrow or supply values for the layer above it, and none may redefine it. Layer 1, Shared core, part of the kit's mechanism: the commands, the evidence schema, the result states, the rule-identifier scheme, and rules and validators that apply to every stack; changed by the kit's maintainers, through a versioned release. Layer 2, Technology profiles, kit mechanism: validators, pinned tool versions, skills, scaffolds and default thresholds for one supported stack; changed by the kit's maintainers, with the teams on that stack. Layer 3, Tool adapters, kit mechanism: one binding per tool the kit runs against; changed by the kit's maintainers, or a team that uses a tool nobody else does. Layer 4, Project configuration, shaded as project meaning: which rules apply, their thresholds, declared exceptions, the chosen profile and adapters, in a committed file reviewed like code; changed by the project. Right: the three commands and where each acts. init acts on the repository: it takes a technology profile and a list of adapters, writes the kit-owned files and a starting project configuration, records the kit version and every file it installed, then runs doctor and one verify. doctor acts on the machine where it runs: it checks that what the checks need is present, namely pinned tools, services and test environments, adapter credentials, a valid project configuration and kit-owned files that match the release; it runs no checks, and it names the checks that will return could_not_run. verify acts on the change: it runs every check the project configuration declares for the change and writes one evidence record in the kit's schema, and the same command runs on a developer's machine, in a coding agent's session and in the pipeline. A credit line names the sources of the adapted terms validator and adapter.
svg.text: Engineering Kit: five parts, four layers, three commands
The parts say what the kit contains, the layers say who may change what, and the commands act on the project.
FIVE PARTS: WHAT THE KIT CONTAINS
Rule registry
Validators
Skills with evals
Evidence schema
Adapters
Joined through rule identifiers: validators, skills and evidence records name the rules in the registry.
FOUR LAYERS: WHO MAY CHANGE WHAT
1 Shared core
KIT MECHANISM
The commands, the evidence schema, the result states, the rule-identifier
scheme, and rules and validators that apply to every stack
Changed by: The kit's maintainers, through a versioned release
narrows or supplies values for the layer above; never redefines it
2 Technology profiles
KIT MECHANISM
Validators, pinned tool versions, skills, scaffolds and default thresholds
for one supported stack
Changed by: The kit's maintainers, with the teams on that stack
narrows or supplies values for the layer above; never redefines it
3 Tool adapters
KIT MECHANISM
One binding per tool the kit runs against
Changed by: The kit's maintainers, or a team that uses a tool nobody else does
narrows or supplies values for the layer above; never redefines it
4 Project configuration
PROJECT MEANING
Which rules apply, their thresholds, declared exceptions, the chosen
profile and adapters; a committed file, reviewed like code
Changed by: The project
THREE COMMANDS: WHERE THEY ACT
init
on the repository
Takes a technology profile and a list of adapters.
Writes the kit-owned files and a starting project
configuration. Records the kit version and every
file it installed. Then runs doctor and one verify.
doctor
on the machine
Checks that what the checks need is present:
pinned tools, services and test environments,
adapter credentials, a valid project configuration,
kit-owned files that match the release. Runs no
checks; names those that will be could_not_run.
verify
on the change
Runs every check the project configuration
declares for the change and writes one evidence
record in the kit's schema. The same command
runs on:
a developer's machine
a coding agent's session
the pipeline
Validators: adapted from Böckeler’s computational sensors (martinfowler.com) · Tool adapters: adapted from Cockburn’s ports and adapters pattern
